      - name: Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework
          key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (per-runner, keyed by the release tag) —
          #    every slot is first-run-warm forever;
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the 15-min
          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
            # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
            # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
            # let one job's rm -f unlink the other's in-flight partial, then
            # both curls interleave bytes into one path.
            ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
            rm -f "$ZIP"
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
              # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
              # engages this loop's retries and the explicit failure below.
              if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                -o "$ZIP" \
                https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                break
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework download failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
              sleep 5
            done
            # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
            # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
            # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
            # as the litertlm download above).
            echo "aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -
            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # Per-arch keychain: both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted
      # runner; a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create
      # emptied it under the other's codesign — errSecInternalComponent /
      # "No certificate found", builds 86).
      - name: Import macOS signing certificate
        id: signing
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "⚠️  No signing certificate found — building unsigned (development only)"
            echo "signed=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "✅ Signing certificate found — importing..."
            security delete-keychain build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
            security create-keychain -p "$MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security default-keychain -s build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security unlock-keychain -p "$MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security set-keychain-settings -t 3600 -u build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security list-keychains -d user -s build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db

            echo "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" | base64 --decode > certificate.p12
            security import certificate.p12 -k build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain \
              -P "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD" \
              -T /usr/bin/codesign \
              -T /usr/bin/productbuild
            security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k "$MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            echo "signed=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

Pitfalls burned time here: (1) a PTY driver using setsid without a controlling tty (TPGID -1) makes isig Ctrl+C vanish — SIGINT never fires, false "Ctrl+C dead" verdicts; use pty.fork() so the child owns the tty. Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. Read the `Failed Reason` field of every linked Test Case. 2. If the failure is caused by a missing token, missing permission, missing secret, or any other access/credential/infra issue that you cannot fix in product code, write `outputs/blocked.json` and stop. Do **not** try to code a fix for an access problem. 3. Only attempt a product-code fix when the failure is a genuine product regression. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for Bug Fixes — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the bug from RCA"] T1["RED: Write a unit test that REPRODUCES the bug
— must describe the exact failure scenario
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum fix to make the reproduction test PASS
— simplest possible change
— do not refactor unrelated code"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— run full suite after every change"] T4{"More edge cases to cover?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next edge case"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([Bug fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["Bug TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more code than needed to fix the bug"] R3["✅ Returned bugs: your fix must differ from the previous attempt"] R4["✅ If the bug involves a loop/collection, add a reproduction case with 2+ items, not only a single-item scenario — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still broken"] R5["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph OUTPUTS["Required outputs for bug development"] O1["outputs/rca.md — write FIRST, update as you learn"] O2["outputs/already_fixed.json — only if bug is genuinely fixed in current code AND tests pass"] O3["outputs/blocked.json — only if fix requires external input/credentials/infra"] O4["outputs/response.md — concise PR description (see formatting_rules.md)"] end subgraph RCA["rca.md format"] R1["## Root Cause Analysis"] R2["**Bug**: one-sentence description"] R3["**Root cause**: exact technical reason — file, function, line"] R4["**Impact**: what is broken and under what conditions"] R5["**Fix approach**: what needs to change and why"] R6["**Previous attempt**: PR #, what changed, why insufficient (only if returned bug)"] R1…

project: (note) Workflow convention (gh-1600, 2026-10-17): the macOS publish legs' mirror-checkout MUST stay an INLINE `run:` script in build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml — NEVER a local composite action (`uses: ./.github/actions/...`). Rationale: local `./` actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE AT STEP TIME; on the persistent self-hosted runners that workspace holds the PREVIOUS run's tree (or nothing), and the checkout step is exactly what materializes it — a local action is missing on the first post-merge run and silently stale afterwards. Other conventions from the same fix: (1) self-hosted macOS-only jobs pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (fa-m5-1's unique registration label; the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` list also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the gh-1600 routing bug); (2) bench-harbor writes harbor output to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs`, never the workspace, and tears shard docker containers down before rm (its cleanup step must declare its own ENV_TYPE — step-scoped env from the harbor-run step is invisible and `set -u` kills an always() step); (3) CI workflow-shape regressions are pinned by static tests parsing the workflow YAML (test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart pattern: workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart / release_hygiene_test.dart precedent). project: (note) Workflow convention (gh-1600, 2026-10-17): the macOS publish legs' mirror-checkout MUST stay an INLINE `run:` script in build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml — NEVER a local composite action (`uses: ./.github/actions/...`). Rationale: local `./` actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE AT STEP TIME; on the persistent self-hosted runners that workspace holds the PREVIOUS run's tree (or nothing), and the checkout step is exactly what materializes it — a local action is missing on the first post-merge run and silently stale afterwards. Other conventions from the same fix: (1) self-hosted macOS-only jobs pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (fa-m5-1's unique registration label; the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` list also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the gh-1600 routing bug); (2) bench-harbor writes harbor output to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs`, never the workspace, and tears shard docker containers down before rm (its cleanup step must declare its own ENV_TYPE — step-scoped env from the harbor-run step is invisible and `set -u` kills an always() step); (3) CI workflow-shape regressions are pinned by static tests parsing the workflow YAML (test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart pattern: workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart / release_hygiene_test.dart precedent). project: (note) CI invariant (gh-1310, 2026-10-06): every flutter_app `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` in .github/workflows MUST ride the shared composite action `.github/actions/flutter-pub-get` — NEVER a bare run-step (`cd flutter_app && flutter pub get ...` trips test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart). Rationale: pub has NO retry for its git-dep mirror clones (flutter_js, flutter_js_widget_runtime); one transient "Connection reset by peer" on github.com:443 kills the leg, and lockfile-refresh release commits (gh-1299 class) cold-miss the flutter-action pub cache so fresh clones happen exactly at release time — that flake red ci.yml build-macos on the very next main run after #1304 fixed the deterministic lockfile drift. Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Rationale: local `./` actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE AT STEP TIME; on the persistent self-hosted runners that workspace holds the PREVIOUS run's tree (or nothing), and the checkout step is exactly what materializes it — a local action is missing on the first post-merge run and silently stale afterwards. Other conventions from the same fix: (1) self-hosted macOS-only jobs pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (fa-m5-1's unique registration label; the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` list also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the gh-1600 routing bug); (2) bench-harbor writes harbor output to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs`, never the workspace, and tears shard docker containers down before rm (its cleanup step must declare its own ENV_TYPE — step-scoped env from the harbor-run step is invisible and `set -u` kills an always() step); (3) CI workflow-shape regressions are pinned by static tests parsing the workflow YAML (test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart pattern: workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart / release_hygiene_test.dart precedent). project: (note) Workflow convention (gh-1600, 2026-10-17): the macOS publish legs' mirror-checkout MUST stay an INLINE `run:` script in build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml — NEVER a local composite action (`uses: ./.github/actions/...`). Rationale: local `./` actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE AT STEP TIME; on the persistent self-hosted runners that workspace holds the PREVIOUS run's tree (or nothing), and the checkout step is exactly what materializes it — a local action is missing on the first post-merge run and silently stale afterwards. Other conventions from the same fix: (1) self-hosted macOS-only jobs pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (fa-m5-1's unique registration label; the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` list also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the gh-1600 routing bug); (2) bench-harbor writes harbor output to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs`, never the workspace, and tears shard docker containers down before rm (its cleanup step must declare its own ENV_TYPE — step-scoped env from the harbor-run step is invisible and `set -u` kills an always() step); (3) CI workflow-shape regressions are pinned by static tests parsing the workflow YAML (test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart pattern: workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart / release_hygiene_test.dart precedent). Resume across runs makes convergence guaranteed-ish: run N downloads ~72MB at 100KB/s... arm64 delivered 71.3MB this run; a fresh run tomorrow resumes from 71.3MB and needs 26MB → ~4.5min → completes. x86_64 (slower, ~40KB/s → ~28.7MB/run) needs ceil(97.2/28.7) ≈ 4 runs. Can we do better? Raise the step timeout AND per-atempt budget. E.g. timeout-minutes: 30, attempts 1..7 × max-time 240 = 1680s of download budget + slack. At 40KB/s → 67MB/run; 2 runs. At 100KB/s → completes in one run (168s×... 97.2MB at 100KB/s = 972s < 1680s ✓). Hmm, 30min step... The step currently 15min. Daily pipeline, self-hosted, one runner: a 30-min download step twice (per arch, sequential-ish) adds wall time to the daily publish. Acceptable? The job itself takes ~25+ min for the rest. Doubling the cap only matters when downloading actually runs (cache hit → skipped entirely).

Alternatively — since both archs need the SAME zip... wait, do they? The xcframework is universal (contains both ios/macos slices?). The zip is ONE asset (~97.2MB = 92.7MiB, the comment says 92.7MB asset ✓). Both arch jobs download the same content but to per-arch paths (to avoid the /tmp race). Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. Read the `Failed Reason` field of every linked Test Case. 2. If the failure is caused by a missing token, missing permission, missing secret, or any other access/credential/infra issue that you cannot fix in product code, write `outputs/blocked.json` and stop. Do **not** try to code a fix for an access problem. 3. Only attempt a product-code fix when the failure is a genuine product regression. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for Bug Fixes — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the bug from RCA"] T1["RED: Write a unit test that REPRODUCES the bug
— must describe the exact failure scenario
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum fix to make the reproduction test PASS
— simplest possible change
— do not refactor unrelated code"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— run full suite after every change"] T4{"More edge cases to cover?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next edge case"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([Bug fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["Bug TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more code than needed to fix the bug"] R3["✅ Returned bugs: your fix must differ from the previous attempt"] R4["✅ If the bug involves a loop/collection, add a reproduction case with 2+ items, not only a single-item scenario — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still broken"] R5["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph OUTPUTS["Required outputs for bug development"] O1["outputs/rca.md — write FIRST, update as you learn"] O2["outputs/already_fixed.json — only if bug is genuinely fixed in current code AND tests pass"] O3["outputs/blocked.json — only if fix requires external input/credentials/infra"] O4["outputs/response.md — concise PR description (see formatting_rules.md)"] end subgraph RCA["rca.md format"] R1["## Root Cause Analysis"] R2["**Bug**: one-sentence description"] R3["**Root cause**: exact technical reason — file, function, line"] R4["**Impact**: what is broken and under what conditions"] R5["**Fix approach**: what needs to change and why"] R6["**Previous attempt**: PR #, what changed, why insufficient (only if returned bug)"] R1…

**Build macOS x86_64:**

KEY OBSERVATION: The "out of" total (Z) SHRINKS across attempts: 97,238,501 → 93,429,090 → 82,337,131. This is the size curl reports for the transfer. If resume were working, the expected total would be full_size minus offset. But it's shrinking by LESS than what was downloaded. Let's compute:

x86_64 attempt 1: full size 97,238,501 (the uncompressed... wait, actually 97,238,501 — hmm, the ticket says 51,70,304 out of 5170304 bytes received... no wait, ticket said 25818587 out of 5170304. Also, importantly: x86_64 shows totals of 97MB, 93MB, 82MB — the ACTUAL WasmRun.xcframework.zip from the wasm_run release. Hmm wait, the workflow comment says "the 92.7MB asset". So the full asset is ~97,238,501 bytes (92.7MiB). 

So the "out of Z" numbers: attempt 1 Z=97,238,501 (full). Attempt 2 Z=93,429,090 — that's 97,238,501 - 3,809,411 = 93,429,090. ✓ That's exactly full minus attempt-1's received bytes! So the offset WAS 3,809,411 attempt 2 — RESUME WORKED for x86_64 attempt 2!

Attempt 3: 97,238,501 - (3,809,411 + 11,091,959) = 97,238,501 - 14,901,370 = 82,337,131 ✓ EXACTLY. So resume worked perfectly! Each attempt continues from where the last stopped.

So the problem is simply SPEED: 
- x86_64: attempt 1 got 3.8MB, attempt 2 got 11.1MB, attempt 3 got 13.8MB. Total: 28.7MB of 97.2MB. Download speed ~16-58KB/s?! At 240s per attempt: 3,809,411/239615 = 15.9KB/s; 11,091,959/239582 = 46.3KB/s; 13,813,416/239625 = 57.6KB/s. That's abysmal — much slower than the ~105KB/s in the ticket excerpt for arm64 attempt 3.
- arm64: attempt 1: 22,757,367/239726 = 94.9KB/s; attempt 2: 22,710,830/239640 = 94.8KB/s; attempt 3: 25,818,587/239708 = 107.7KB/s. Total across attempts: 22.8+22.7+25.8 = 71.3MB of 97.2MB. Still short by ~26MB!

So resume WORKS, but the link speed (~95-108KB/s for arm64) means each 240s attempt gets only ~24MB, and 3 attempts = ~72MB < 97.2MB needed. The budget math in the comment assumed ~300KB/s ("it needs ~309s" for 92.7MB → 309s ≈ 92.7MB at ~315KB/s). The link is 3x slower than assumed.

Also both jobs run CONCURRENTLY on the same self-hosted runner (per-arch zip paths to avoid the race), so they share bandwidth — each sees ~half. x86_64 saw even worse (16-58KB/s) — maybe the runner's uplink was saturated by both jobs plus... interesting, arm64 got ~95-108KB/s while x86_64 got ~16-58KB/s — not symmetric; maybe the two jobs at different times: x86_64 attempts ran 19:03→19:15, arm64 attempts 19:16→19:28 (after x86_64 finished failing). Actually from timestamps: x86_64 step started ~19:03:01, attempts timed out at 19:07:01, 19:11:07, 19:15:12. arm64 step started ~19:16:49, attempts at 19:20:49, 19:24:54, 19:28:59. They were NOT concurrent during downloads — x86_64's download phase ended before arm64's began. But the speeds differ wildly anyway (16-58 vs 95-108 KB/s). Whatever — the uplink to github release CDN is just very slow right now.

Also worth noting: THE DAILY RUN. This is the daily-publish pipeline. Let me check the daily-publish.yml to see what it does with build-macos.yml. And gh-1149 was the previous fix that introduced this loop. The ticket auto-closes when the leg goes green.

So the root cause: the per-atempt --max-time 240 × 3 attempts budget (720s of download) can only deliver ~72MB at the observed ~100KB/s link speed, but the asset is 97.2MB (92.7MiB) — the arithmetic assumed ~300KB/s. Resume works, but total download budget is insufficient. Additionally the /tmp partial zip is deleted on each run start (`rm -f "$ZIP"`), so progress doesn't persist ACROSS step retries — a full re-run starts from 0.

Wait, actually, let me double check whether there's an earlier partial from previous failed daily runs that could be resumed: the rm -f kills it. The actions/cache would save... the cache step saves only if the JOB succeeds (actions/cache default: post step saves on job success). Job failed → cache not saved. So every daily run re-downloads from 0.

Now — what's the right fix?

Constraints:
- Step timeout-minutes: 15 = 900s.
- Need 97.2MB at observed worst-case ~16KB/s?? That's not feasible in 900s (would need 97.2MB at 16KB/s = 6075s). But x86_64's slowness might because both jobs... no wait, they didn't overlap during downloads. Hmm, x86_64 avg over 3 attempts: 28.7MB/720s ≈ 40KB/s. arm64: 71.3MB/720s ≈ 99KB/s.

Hmm, so link speed varies wildly (40-100KB/s observed this run). At 100KB/s, 97.2MB needs ~972s > 900s step cap in a SINGLE run. Even with perfect within-step resume, the whole 15-minute step can't deliver the file at 100KB/s. So a within-step-only fix cannot guarantee success.

Options:

**A. Persist the partial zip across runs** on the self-hosted runner. /tmp persists across runs on a self-hosted runner (it's a long-lived machine — "/Users/uladzimir_klyshevich/actions-runner-yoloit"). Instead of `rm -f "$ZIP"`, RESUME from any existing partial (keep per-arch paths). Then each daily run makes forward progress; after enough runs the file completes, gets unzipped, and the actions/cache post-step saves it (job succeeds → cache saved) → future runs hit cache. But wait — if the download loop succeeds mid-run, the job succeeds and cache saves the FRAMEWORK (path: vendor/.../WasmRun.xcframework). But there's a catch: the cache action's post step runs at END of job — but the vendor path is inside the checked-out workspace... The cache step: path: vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework. Post-step tars it up. Fine.

But relying on cross-run partial persistence is slow-to-converge (each run adds ~70MB... actually at 100KB/s per 900s step → 90MB per run — one run could nearly finish at 100KB/s). Hmm, but at 40KB/s (x86_64 this run) a 900s step delivers 36MB → needs 3 consecutive runs to accumulate 97MB. Meh but converges. Risk: zip partial becomes stale/corupt? The digest check at the end protects correctness. Partial zips resumable indefinitely. But accumulating across MULTIPLE daily runs means the leg stays red for days — the pipeline auto-closes when green; daily runs would eventually converge. Clunky but robust.

**arm64:**
- Attempt 1: resumed from 0, timed out at 239726ms having received 22,757,367 of 97,238,501 (full size) → speed ~94.9KB/s
- Attempt 2: "Resuming transfer from byte position 22757367" (94,810,134 remaining → "out of 74,481,134"... wait: 97,238,501 − 22,757,367 = 74,481,134 ✓), received 22,710,830 → position 45,468,197
- Attempt 3: "Resuming transfer from byte position 45468197" (97,238,501 − 45,468,197 = 51,70,304 ✓ matches "out of 51,70,304"), received 25,818,587 → position 71,286,784 of 97,238,501. Timed out. Failed after 3 attempts: still 25,951,717 bytes short (26.7%).

So: resume works flawlessly; the link is just slow (~95-108KB/s), so 3 × 240s = 720s of download only delivers ~71MB of the 97.2MB asset. The gh-1149 budget comment assumed ~300KB/s ("92.7MB needs ~309s") — actual measured is 3× slower.

x86_64 was even slower: 28.7MB of 97.2MB total across 720s (~40KB/s avg — variable).

To COMPLETE at the observed worst speed within the step: 97.2MB at ~40KB/s = 2,430s = 40min. That exceeds any sane step cap. So a single-run fix cannot guarantee completion at these speeds. We need the partial zip to PERSIST across runs, so each run resumes from where the last one left off, converging to completion, and then:
1. unzip → framework in place → job green
2. actions/cache post-step saves the framework (job success) → future runs hit the cache and skip downloading entirely.

Wait — but there's a subtlety: the cache step "Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework" has key `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0`. When there's no cache hit, the post-step (save) runs at end of job and saves IF the job succeeds. Good.

Second subtlety: does /tmp persist across runs on this self-hosted runner? It's a long-lived machine ("/Users/uladzimir_klyshevich/actions-runner-yoloit"). /tmp on macOS is periodically cleaned by the OS (files older than 3 days) but daily runs are fine. The per-arch zip path exists to avoid the two jobs racing. If both jobs keep partials and both make progress each daily run, both converge.

BUT: currently the script does `rm -f "$ZIP"` before the loop — deliberately discarding any stale partial. Why? Probably to avoid resuming a partial from a DIFFERENT asset version (if the release asset were re-uploaded, resume would corrupt). Protection: the shasum digest check AFTER download catches any corruption before unzip. So keeping the partial is safe: worst case, resume from a stale/incompatible partial fails the digest → exit 1 → but then... hmm, it would fail FOREVER (every run resumes the same corrupt partial). Mitigation: on digest failure, rm the partial and... within the same step you can retry once from scratch. Or better: verify the partial's already-downloaded prefix? Can't cheaply.

Hmm, actually, let me reconsider. What's the probability the upstream asset changes? The URL pins a tag (wasm_run-v0.1.0) and release assets are immutable per the existing comment. The digest check pins content. Corupt-partial-forever risk is mainly from disk corruption — negligible. And a human can rm /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-*.zip if it ever wedges. I'll note it in the comment.

Third subtlety: If the partial completes exactly to full size but the loop's LAST attempt timed out at position < full, next run resumes at position == full → curl with -C - and a complete file: curl errors with "416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable"? Actually curl -C - with a complete file: it sends Range: bytes=<size>- and server returns 416, curl error 33 (HTTP RANGE error) with --fail → loop fails all 3 attempts → exit 1 even though the zip is complete!

Wait, actually — curl has a special case: when the file is already fully downloaded with -C - and the server says 416... curl returns error 33. Hmm, but modern curl (7.5x+) treats "already have entire file" specially? There was a change: curl 7.19... no. Let me think. `curl -C -o f url` where f is complete: curl sends the Range request; GitHub S3 returns 416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable; with --fail curl exits 22. Hmm, actually for 416 curl emits error 33 "HTTP server doesn't seem to support byte ranges" or exit 22 via --fail. Either way, failure.

BUT in the current flow, would we ever reach the loop with a COMPLETE zip? The loop `break`s on success, then digest+unzip happen in the same step. The complete zip remains at /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-<arch>.zip after success. Next run: framework comes from actions/cache hit (if cache saved) → the download branch isn't even entered. If cache MISED (e.g., runner re-registered, cache evicted) but /tmp zip complete → enters download branch → curl -C - fails on 416 → after 3 attempts → exit 1. BAD.

Handle it: before the loop, if the zip already exists AND its size == expected... we don't know expected size a priori. Alternatives: digest-check an existing complete zip BEFORE the loop (if shasum matches → skip download entirely). That's clean:

```bash
ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${ matrix.arch }}.zip"
EXPECTED_SHA="aca903d7..."
if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$EXPECTED_SHA $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 echo "Complete zip already present (resumed across runs) — skipping download"
else
 ... loop (no rm -f, resume partial) ...
 digest check (hard fail)
fi
unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
``

Hmm wait, but if the digest fails at the end after a successful download (asset changed upstream), currently: `shasum -c` fails → set -e → exit 1. Fine, human intervention needed anyway (new digest). 

Now, what about the per-atempt budget within the step? Keep max-time 240 × 3 attempts = 720s + sleeps 10s + unzip ~within 900s cap. Resume across runs makes convergence guaranteed-ish: run N downloads ~72MB at 100KB/s... arm64 delivered 71.3MB this run; a fresh run tomorrow resumes from 71.3MB and needs 26MB → ~4.5min → completes. x86_64 (slower, ~40KB/s → ~28.7MB/run) needs ceil(97.2/28.7) ≈ 4 runs. Hmm — that means the leg stays red for up to ~4 daily runs. That's slow convergence but each daily run makes progress.

Can we do better? Raise the step timeout AND per-atempt budget. E.g. timeout-minutes: 30, attempts 1..7 × max-time 240 = 1680s of download budget + slack. At 40KB/s → 67MB/run; 2 runs. At 100KB/s → completes in one run (168s×... 97.2MB at 100KB/s = 972s < 1680s ✓). Hmm, 30min step... The step currently 15min. Daily pipeline, self-hosted, one runner: a 30-min download step twice (per arch, sequential-ish) adds wall time to the daily publish. Acceptable? The job itself takes ~25+ min for the rest. Doubling the cap only matters when downloading actually runs (cache hit → skipped entirely).

Alternatively — since both archs need the SAME zip... wait, do they? The xcframework is universal (contains both ios/macos slices?). The zip is ONE asset (~97.2MB = 92.7MiB, the comment says 92.7MB asset ✓). Both arch jobs download the same content but to per-arch paths (to avoid the /tmp race). If the first job completes and... the framework gets cached under key wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 — but per-runner, and both jobs run on the SAME runner but different runner instances? "both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted runner" — the same machine, but are they the same runner registration (job slots)? actions/cache is scoped per runner? No — actions/cache backend is GitHub's cache service, keyed by repo+branch, NOT runner. But on SELF-HOSTED... the cache is still stored remotely by GitHub (or ACTIONS_CACHE_URL if a cache server is configured). Hmm — with a self-hosted runner, actions/cache uses GitHub's cache service unless configured otherwise; cache entries are per-repo+ref+scope. Both jobs SHOULD hit the same cache once saved... 

But wait — the cache is only SAVED when a job succeeds AND there was a miss. First green run: whichever arch job succeeds first saves the framework; the other job (already running concurrently or after) may miss the cache (saved mid-run? cache save happens in post step at job end — the other job started before that → miss) and do its own download. Subsequent runs: both hit.

Hmm, but do both jobs hit the same cache key? Yes: same key string, same repo/ref. Self-hosted runners CAN use GitHub cache service if the repo allows cache for... …

Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. Read the `Failed Reason` field of every linked Test Case. 2. If the failure is caused by a missing token, missing permission, missing secret, or any other access/credential/infra issue that you cannot fix in product code, write `outputs/blocked.json` and stop. Do **not** try to code a fix for an access problem. 3. Only attempt a product-code fix when the failure is a genuine product regression. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for Bug Fixes — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the bug from RCA"] T1["RED: Write a unit test that REPRODUCES the bug
— must describe the exact failure scenario
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum fix to make the reproduction test PASS
— simplest possible change
— do not refactor unrelated code"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— run full suite after every change"] T4{"More edge cases to cover?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next edge case"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([Bug fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["Bug TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more code than needed to fix the bug"] R3["✅ Returned bugs: your fix must differ from the previous attempt"] R4["✅ If the bug involves a loop/collection, add a reproduction case with 2+ items, not only a single-item scenario — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still broken"] R5["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph OUTPUTS["Required outputs for bug development"] O1["outputs/rca.md — write FIRST, update as you learn"] O2["outputs/already_fixed.json — only if bug is genuinely fixed in current code AND tests pass"] O3["outputs/blocked.json — only if fix requires external input/credentials/infra"] O4["outputs/response.md — concise PR description (see formatting_rules.md)"] end subgraph RCA["rca.md format"] R1["## Root Cause Analysis"] R2["**Bug**: one-sentence description"] R3["**Root cause**: exact technical reason — file, function, line"] R4["**Impact**: what is broken and under what conditions"] R5["**Fix approach**: what needs to change and why"] R6["**Previous attempt**: PR #, what changed, why insufficient (only if returned bug)"] R1…

10 memories found:
project: (note) Workflow convention (gh-1600, 2026-10-17): the macOS publish legs' mirror-checkout MUST stay an INLINE `run:` script in build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml — NEVER a local composite action (`uses: ./.github/actions/...`). Rationale: local `./` actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE AT STEP TIME; on the persistent self-hosted runners that workspace holds the PREVIOUS run's tree (or nothing), and the checkout step is exactly what materializes it — a local action is missing on the first post-merge run and silently stale afterwards. Other conventions from the same fix: (1) self-hosted macOS-only jobs pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (fa-m5-1's unique registration label; the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` list also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the gh-1600 routing bug); (2) bench-harbor writes harbor output to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs`, never the workspace, and tears shard docker containers down before rm (its cleanup step must declare its own ENV_TYPE — step-scoped env from the harbor-run step is invisible and `set -u` kills an always() step); (3) CI workflow-shape regressions are pinned by static tests parsing the workflow YAML (test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart pattern: workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart / release_hygiene_test.dart precedent). [#note,#source_agent,ci,workflows,self-hosted-runner,composite-actions,gh-1600,convention]
project: (note) flutter_agent_harness (GitHub IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, pub.dev package) releases: version bump in pubspec triggers tag CI that publishes to pub.dev and builds CLI binaries for linux/macos/windows plus macOS DMG, iOS TestFlight, and web Pages; Android is disabled. [#note,#source_agent,ci,pubdev]
project: (note) Release pipeline: build-macos.yml auto-increments version and tags (creating the GitHub Release with CLI tarballs + macOS dmg/zip), build-mobile.yml does iOS/TestFlight on a self-hosted runner, pages.yml deploys web to https://fa1.dev/app/; tag push should trigger pub.dev publish via ci.yml OIDC but pub.dev latest lags far behind (publish job not firing). [#note,#source_agent,ci,workflows]
project: (note) CI invariant (gh-1310, 2026-10-06): every flutter_app `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` in .github/workflows MUST ride the shared composite action `.github/actions/flutter-pub-get` — NEVER a bare run-step (`cd flutter_app && flutter pub get ...` trips test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart). Rationale: pub has NO retry for its git-dep mirror clones (flutter_js, flutter_js_widget_runtime); one transient "Connection reset by peer" on github.com:443 kills the leg, and lockfile-refresh release commits (gh-1299 class) cold-miss the flutter-action pub cache so fresh clones happen exactly at release time — that flake red ci.yml build-macos on the very next main run after #1304 fixed the deterministic lockfile drift. The action carries the #726 bounded retry (3 attempts, 15s backoff) + deterministic-skew fail-fast ("Unable to satisfy ... pubspec.lock" = exit immediately, don't blame the network). Scripts (tag_release.sh, build_browser_ext.sh, build_office_addin.sh) keep their own invocations — they ride the warm pub cache after a workflow-level action step resolved first; and every workflow path that reaches flutter_app now resolves through the action FIRST (gh-1310 rework, 2026-10-06): ci.yml release-tag warms the cache with the action before bash scripts/tag_release.sh (its pre-tag enforce-lockfile smoke stays in the script per release_hygiene NG2/AC3 but is no longer a cold, unretried resolution), and office-addin.yml resolves before the first flutter consumer (Chrome boot tests) so flutter test's implicit pub get never fires first. Diagnosing tag-run reds: exit 65 = enforce-lockfile skew (gh-1299/#1304), exit 69 = pub git-clone error (transient, now retried); gh-1299's lockfile-drift incident also felled the pure-Dart legs via test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart AC2. [#note,#source_agent,ci,pub-get,retry,gh-1310,gh-726,flaky,workflow]
project: (note) CI/CD for the Chrome extension: the Pages workflow builds it and publishes to fa1.dev, the macOS release pipeline attaches a build to the GitHub Release, and the landing page carries install instructions. [#note,#source_agent,fa1.dev,release]
project: (note) fa_widgets catalog initiative (2026-08): repo /Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/fa_widgets (git@github.com:IstiN/fa_widgets.git, MIT). Master spec = flutter_agent/docs/widgets/GOAL.md. Sources-only in git (no binaries); CI builds zips + rolling release 'catalog' via stable URLs github.com/IstiN/fa_widgets/releases/latest/download/{catalog.json,<id>-<version>.zip}; per-widget immutable tags <id>-v<version> on version bump. No submodule. CLI out of scope until after App Store submission. Zip layout: single root folder <id>/ inside each zip. M0 scope: Dart tooling (validate/catalog gen), workflows validate.yml+publish.yml, seed widgets calculator+focus-timer. Site gallery page site/widgets planned (client-side fetch of catalog.json). Analytics: GitHub asset counts (repo), page counters (site), AppAnalytics events widget_* (app phase). [#note,#source_agent,fa-widgets,catalog,release-workflow,widgets]
project: (note) gh-1054 rework round 3: "Quality gate" in ci_failures.md is only the AGGREGATE — fetch per-leg results via `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/runs/<id>/jobs --paginate --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'` (logs need `--allow-escape-sequences`); on this round the real legs were Static gates + Core shard 0 + PTY shards 0/1. The #1 Static-gates breaker is the repo-wide 2800-line file cap (`find lib test example -name '*.dart' ... -gt 2800`, scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh MAX_LINES) — agent_loop.dart (3179) was fixed by extracting the stuck-supervision subsystem (~650 lines) into a `part of` file `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` (agent_cli.dart's 10 part files are the repo convention); builtin_tools.dart (2803) by moving the soft-yield hand-back text builder into stuck_tool.dart as `stuckBackgroundHandbackText` (re-exported via agent_loop.dart's `export 'stuck_tool.dart' show` list). Also: `dart analyze` at repo root fails with office_addin errors until `cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get` — pre-existing local-env artifact, not a branch break (CI passes because its checkout resolves it). CI flake triage recipe: compare the failing test against main's LATEST green ci.yml run on the SAME sha (gh api workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=main) — main's own runs flake on different legs (redact/perf_test.dart), proving runner-load flakiness. AC5 REPL-parity flake fix pattern: never poll a growing session JSONL via JsonlSessionRepo from outside (repo.open takes the lock the live REPL appends under every heartbeat — 50ms polling starves the watched leg, exhausting even a 90s budget); poll the raw file text for the terminal record (`"action":"escalate"`) at 250ms cadence instead, and compare collapsed heartbeat runs (consecutive same-attempt heartbeats → one) not raw counts. [#note,#source_agent,source_agent,ci,gotcha,gh-1054,quality-gate]

blocks.text:
Now completely clear:

**arm64:**
- Attempt 1: resumed from 0, timed out at 239726ms having received 22,757,367 of 97,238,501 (full size) → speed ~94.9KB/s
- Attempt 2: "Resuming transfer from byte position 22757367" (94,810,134 remaining → "out of 74,481,134"... wait: 97,238,501 − 22,757,367 = 74,481,134 ✓), received 22,710,830 → position 45,468,197
- Attempt 3: "Resuming transfer from byte position 45468197" (97,238,501 − 45,468,197 = 51,70,304 ✓ matches "out of 51,70,304"), received 25,818,587 → position 71,286,784 of 97,238,501. Timed out. Failed after 3 attempts: still 25,951,717 bytes short (26.7%).

So: resume works flawlessly; the link is just slow (~95-108KB/s), so 3 × 240s = 720s of download only delivers ~71MB of the 97.2MB asset. The gh-1149 budget comment assumed ~300KB/s ("92.7MB needs ~309s") — actual measured is 3× slower.

x86_64 was even slower: 28.7MB of 97.2MB total across 720s (~40KB/s avg — variable).

To COMPLETE at the observed worst speed within the step: 97.2MB at ~40KB/s = 2,430s = 40min. That exceeds any sane step cap. So a single-run fix cannot guarantee completion at these speeds. We need the partial zip to PERSIST across runs, so each run resumes from where the last one left off, converging to completion, and then:
1. unzip → framework in place → job green
2. actions/cache post-step saves the framework (job success) → future runs hit the cache and skip downloading entirely.

Wait — but there's a subtlety: the cache step "Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework" has key `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0`. When there's no cache hit, the post-step (save) runs at end of job and saves IF the job succeeds. Good.

Second subtlety: does /tmp persist across runs on this self-hosted runner? It's a long-lived machine ("/Users/uladzimir_klyshevich/actions-runner-yoloit"). /tmp on macOS is periodically cleaned by the OS (files older than 3 days) but daily runs are fine. The per-arch zip path exists to avoid the two jobs racing. If both jobs keep partials and both make progress each daily run, both converge.

BUT: currently the script does `rm -f "$ZIP"` before the loop — deliberately discarding any stale partial. Why? Probably to avoid resuming a partial from a DIFFERENT asset version (if the release asset were re-uploaded, resume would corrupt). Protection: the shasum digest check AFTER download catches any corruption before unzip. So keeping the partial is safe: worst case, resume from a stale/incompatible partial fails the digest → exit 1 → but then... hmm, it would fail FOREVER (every run resumes the same corrupt partial). Mitigation: on digest failure, rm the partial and... within the same step you can retry once from scratch. Or better: verify the partial's already-downloaded prefix? Can't cheaply.

Hmm, actually, let me reconsider. What's the probability the upstream asset changes? The URL pins a tag (wasm_run-v0.1.0) and release assets are immutable per the existing comment. The digest check pins content. Corupt-partial-forever risk is mainly from disk corruption — negligible. And a human can rm /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-*.zip if it ever wedges. I'll note it in the comment.

Third subtlety: If the partial completes exactly to full size but the loop's LAST attempt timed out at position < full, next run resumes at position == full → curl with -C - and a complete file: curl errors with "416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable"? Actually curl -C - with a complete file: it sends Range: bytes=<size>- and server returns 416, curl error 33 (HTTP RANGE error) with --fail → loop fails all 3 attempts → exit 1 even though the zip is complete!

Wait, actually — curl has a special case: when the file is already fully downloaded with -C - and the server says 416... curl returns error 33. Hmm, but modern curl (7.5x+) treats "already have entire file" specially? There was a change: curl 7.19... no. Let me think. `curl -C -o f url` where f is complete: curl sends the Range request; GitHub S3 returns 416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable; with --fail curl exits 22. Hmm, actually for 416 curl emits error 33 "HTTP server doesn't seem to support byte ranges" or exit 22 via --fail. Either way, failure.

BUT in the current flow, would we ever reach the loop with a COMPLETE zip? The loop `break`s on success, then digest+unzip happen in the same step. The complete zip remains at /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-<arch>.zip after success. Next run: framework comes from actions/cache hit (if cache saved) → the download branch isn't even entered. If cache MISED (e.g., runner re-registered, cache evicted) but /tmp zip complete → enters download branch → curl -C - fails on 416 → after 3 attempts → exit 1. BAD.

Handle it: before the loop, if the zip already exists AND its size == expected... we don't know expected size a priori. Alternatives: digest-check an existing complete zip BEFORE the loop (if shasum matches → skip download entirely). That's clean:

```bash
ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${ matrix.arch }}.zip"
EXPECTED_SHA="aca903d7..."
if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$EXPECTED_SHA $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 echo "Complete zip already present (resumed across runs) — skipping download"
else
 ... loop (no rm -f, resume partial) ...
 digest check (hard fail)
fi
unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
``

Hmm wait, but if the digest fails at the end after a successful download (asset changed upstream), currently: `shasum -c` fails → set -e → exit 1. Fine, human intervention needed anyway (new digest). 

Now, what about the per-atempt budget within the step? Keep max-time 240 × 3 attempts = 720s + sleeps 10s + unzip ~within 900s cap. Resume across runs makes convergence guaranteed-ish: run N downloads ~72MB at 100KB/s... arm64 delivered 71.3MB this run; a fresh run tomorrow resumes from 71.3MB and needs 26MB → ~4.5min → completes. x86_64 (slower, ~40KB/s → ~28.7MB/run) needs ceil(97.2/28.7) ≈ 4 runs. Hmm — that means the leg stays red for up to ~4 daily runs. That's slow convergence but each daily run makes progress.

Can we do better? Raise the step timeout AND per-atempt budget. E.g. timeout-minutes: 30, attempts 1..7 × max-time 240 = 1680s of download budget + slack. At 40KB/s → 67MB/run; 2 runs. At 100KB/s → completes in one run (168s×... 97.2MB at 100KB/s = 972s < 1680s ✓). Hmm, 30min step... The step currently 15min. Daily pipeline, self-hosted, one runner: a 30-min download step twice (per arch, sequential-ish) adds wall time to the daily publish. Acceptable? The job itself takes ~25+ min for the rest. Doubling the cap only matters when downloading actually runs (cache hit → skipped entirely).

Alternatively — since both archs need the SAME zip... wait, do they? The xcframework is universal (contains both ios/macos slices?). The zip is ONE asset (~97.2MB = 92.7MiB, the comment says 92.7MB asset ✓). Both arch jobs download the same content but to per-arch paths (to avoid the /tmp race). If the first job completes and... the framework gets cached under key wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 — but per-runner, and both jobs run on the SAME runner but different runner instances? "both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted runner" — the same machine, but are they the same runner registration (job slots)? actions/cache is scoped per runner? No — actions/cache backend is GitHub's cache service, keyed by repo+branch, NOT runner. But on SELF-HOSTED... the cache is still stored remotely by GitHub (or ACTIONS_CACHE_URL if a cache server is configured). Hmm — with a self-hosted runner, actions/cache uses GitHub's cache service unless configured otherwise; cache entries are per-repo+ref+scope. Both jobs SHOULD hit the same cache once saved... 

But wait — the cache is only SAVED when a job succeeds AND there was a miss. First green run: whichever arch job succeeds first saves the framework; the other job (already running concurrently or after) may miss the cache (saved mid-run? cache save happens in post step at job end — the other job started before that → miss) and do its own download. Subsequent runs: both hit.

Hmm, but do both jobs hit the same cache key? Yes: same key string, same repo/ref. Self-hosted runners CAN use GitHub cache service if the repo allows cache for... …

The picture is now fully clear. Resume works perfectly ("Resuming transfer from byte position 45468197"), but the link is ~95-108KB/s — 3×240s delivers only ~71MB of the 97.2MB asset. Let me check the daily-publish workflow and the guard tests that pin this step's shape.

Rationale: local `./` actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE AT STEP TIME; on the persistent self-hosted runners that workspace holds the PREVIOUS run's tree (or nothing), and the checkout step is exactly what materializes it — a local action is missing on the first post-merge run and silently stale afterwards. **arm64:**
- Attempt 1: resumed from 0, timed out at 239726ms having received 22,757,367 of 97,238,501 (full size) → speed ~94.9KB/s
- Attempt 2: "Resuming transfer from byte position 22757367" (94,810,134 remaining → "out of 74,481,134"... wait: 97,238,501 − 22,757,367 = 74,481,134 ✓), received 22,710,830 → position 45,468,197

So: resume works flawlessly; the link is just slow (~95-108KB/s), so 3 × 240s = 720s of download only delivers ~71MB of the 97.2MB asset. The gh-1149 budget comment assumed ~300KB/s ("92.7MB needs ~309s") — actual measured is 3× slower.

x86_64 was even slower: 28.7MB of 97.2MB total across 720s (~40KB/s avg — variable).

To COMPLETE at the observed worst speed within the step: 97.2MB at ~40KB/s = 2,430s = 40min. That exceeds any sane step cap. So a single-run fix cannot guarantee completion at these speeds. We need the partial zip to PERSIST across runs, so each run resumes from where the last one left off, converging to completion, and then:
1. unzip → framework in place → job green
2. actions/cache post-step saves the framework (job success) → future runs hit the cache and skip downloading entirely.

Wait — but there's a subtlety: the cache step "Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework" has key `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0`. When there's no cache hit, the post-step (save) runs at end of job and saves IF the job succeeds. Good.

Second subtlety: does /tmp persist across runs on this self-hosted runner? It's a long-lived machine ("/Users/uladzimir_klyshevich/actions-runner-yoloit"). /tmp on macOS is periodically cleaned by the OS (files older than 3 days) but daily runs are fine. The per-arch zip path exists to avoid the two jobs racing. If both jobs keep partials and both make progress each daily run, both converge.

BUT: currently the script does `rm -f "$ZIP"` before the loop — deliberately discarding any stale partial. Why? Probably to avoid resuming a partial from a DIFFERENT asset version (if the release asset were re-uploaded, resume would corrupt). Protection: the shasum digest check AFTER download catches any corruption before unzip. So keeping the partial is safe: worst case, resume from a stale/incompatible partial fails the digest → exit 1 → but then... hmm, it would fail FOREVER (every run resumes the same corrupt partial). Mitigation: on digest failure, rm the partial and... within the same step you can retry once from scratch. Or better: verify the partial's already-downloaded prefix? Can't cheaply.

Hmm, actually, let me reconsider. What's the probability the upstream asset changes? The URL pins a tag (wasm_run-v0.1.0) and release assets are immutable per the existing comment. The digest check pins content. Corupt-partial-forever risk is mainly from disk corruption — negligible. And a human can rm /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-*.zip if it ever wedges. I'll note it in the comment.

Third subtlety: If the partial completes exactly to full size but the loop's LAST attempt timed out at position < full, next run resumes at position == full → curl with -C - and a complete file: curl errors with "416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable"? Actually curl -C - with a complete file: it sends Range: bytes=<size>- and server returns 416, curl error 33 (HTTP RANGE error) with --fail → loop fails all 3 attempts → exit 1 even though the zip is complete!

Wait, actually — curl has a special case: when the file is already fully downloaded with -C - and the server says 416... curl returns error 33. Hmm, but modern curl (7.5x+) treats "already have entire file" specially? There was a change: curl 7.19... no. Let me think. `curl -C -o f url` where f is complete: curl sends the Range request; GitHub S3 returns 416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable; with --fail curl exits 22. Hmm, actually for 416 curl emits error 33 "HTTP server doesn't seem to support byte ranges" or exit 22 via --fail. Either way, failure.

BUT in the current flow, would we ever reach the loop with a COMPLETE zip? The loop `break`s on success, then digest+unzip happen in the same step. The complete zip remains at /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-<arch>.zip after success. Next run: framework comes from actions/cache hit (if cache saved) → the download branch isn't even entered. If cache MISED (e.g., runner re-registered, cache evicted) but /tmp zip complete → enters download branch → curl -C - fails on 416 → after 3 attempts → exit 1. BAD.

Handle it: before the loop, if the zip already exists AND its size == expected... we don't know expected size a priori. Alternatives: digest-check an existing complete zip BEFORE the loop (if shasum matches → skip download entirely). That's clean:

```bash
ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${ matrix.arch }}.zip"
EXPECTED_SHA="aca903d7..."
if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$EXPECTED_SHA $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 echo "Complete zip already present (resumed across runs) — skipping download"
else
 ... loop (no rm -f, resume partial) ...
 digest check (hard fail)
fi
unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
``

Hmm wait, but if the digest fails at the end after a successful download (asset changed upstream), currently: `shasum -c` fails → set -e → exit 1. Fine, human intervention needed anyway (new digest). 

Now, what about the per-atempt budget within the step? Keep max-time 240 × 3 attempts = 720s + sleeps 10s + unzip ~within 900s cap. Resume across runs makes convergence guaranteed-ish: run N downloads ~72MB at 100KB/s... arm64 delivered 71.3MB this run; a fresh run tomorrow resumes from 71.3MB and needs 26MB → ~4.5min → completes. x86_64 (slower, ~40KB/s → ~28.7MB/run) needs ceil(97.2/28.7) ≈ 4 runs. Hmm — that means the leg stays red for up to ~4 daily runs. That's slow convergence but each daily run makes progress.

Can we do better? Raise the step timeout AND per-atempt budget. E.g. timeout-minutes: 30, attempts 1..7 × max-time 240 = 1680s of download budget + slack. At 40KB/s → 67MB/run; 2 runs. At 100KB/s → completes in one run (168s×... 97.2MB at 100KB/s = 972s < 1680s ✓). Hmm, 30min step... The step currently 15min. Daily pipeline, self-hosted, one runner: a 30-min download step twice (per arch, sequential-ish) adds wall time to the daily publish. Acceptable? The job itself takes ~25+ min for the rest. Doubling the cap only matters when downloading actually runs (cache hit → skipped entirely).

Alternatively — since both archs need the SAME zip... wait, do they? The xcframework is universal (contains both ios/macos slices?). The zip is ONE asset (~97.2MB = 92.7MiB, the comment says 92.7MB asset ✓). Both arch jobs download the same content but to per-arch paths (to avoid the /tmp race). If the first job completes and... the framework gets cached under key wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 — but per-runner, and both jobs run on the SAME runner but different runner instances? "both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted runner" — the same machine, but are they the same runner registration (job slots)? actions/cache is scoped per runner? No — actions/cache backend is GitHub's cache service, keyed by repo+branch, NOT runner. But on SELF-HOSTED... the cache is still stored remotely by GitHub (or ACTIONS_CACHE_URL if a cache server is configured). Hmm — with a self-hosted runner, actions/cache uses GitHub's cache service unless configured otherwise; cache entries are per-repo+ref+scope. Both jobs SHOULD hit the same cache once saved... 

But wait — the cache is only SAVED when a job succeeds AND there was a miss. First green run: whichever arch job succeeds first saves the framework; the other job (already running concurrently or after) may miss the cache (saved mid-run? cache save happens in post step at job end — the other job started before that → miss) and do its own download. Subsequent runs: both hit.

Hmm, but do both jobs hit the same cache key? Yes: same key string, same repo/ref. Self-hosted runners CAN use GitHub cache service if the repo allows cache for... …

The picture is now fully clear. Resume works perfectly ("Resuming transfer from byte position 45468197"), but the link is ~95-108KB/s — 3×240s delivers only ~71MB of the 97.2MB asset. Let me check the daily-publish workflow and the guard tests that pin this step's shape.
